provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: This family grows a path from each seed (colour 2) on the bottom edge. Each step goes up when the cell above is not an obstacle (5). If the cell above is an obstacle, the path sidesteps one cell right. It keeps sidestepping until the cell above is clear, then climbs again. The path stops when it moves past the top edge. It also stops when a sidestep would leave the grid or land on an obstacle. Every cell the path enters is painted 2. This matches the constructor's draw loop and the archived transform. The factory sends the original 'up' vector (-1,0) and 'right' vector (0,1) through the D4 transform: for indices 4 and above it negates the column component, then applies the clockwise rotation (dr,dc)->(dc,-dr) d4%4 times. It bakes those direction vectors into the emitted program as constants. The colour roles are also constants: obstacle=palette[5], seed=palette[2] (background palette[0] is implied). The emitted solver works directly in visible coordinates. It finds seeds as seed-coloured cells on the edge where one step against the growth direction leaves the grid. It sorts them along the sidestep axis, matching the original left-to-right order. Then it walks each path with the rotated up/right moves and the same stop conditions. Rectangular grids work because all bounds checks are generic.
draft_notes.limitations: I have not run any tests. Seed detection relies on the constructor domain: seeds lie only on the original bottom edge, and no other seed-coloured cells sit on that edge. The original seeds are in columns 1..W-2, so corner ambiguity cannot arise. Constructor notes for host review: (1) The generator rejects any scene where a path would step into an existing 2 (the 'output must be red' branch) or where a seed's left neighbour is already 2. The archived solver and this program do not reject such scenes; they just keep walking, which affects no valid generated scene. (2) Under the generator's constraints, paths never step through an existing 2 while climbing, so seed processing order cannot change the result. Sorting is kept only for fidelity. (3) The generator guards output[r-1][c] at r==0 with 'r == 0 or ...', so Python's negative-index wraparound has no effect, and the 'c - 1' seed check is safe because seeds are never in column 0. I found no contradictions between the fixtures and the rule.
